'''Nicholas''' ('''Nikolaos''') '''Athanasiou Peppas''' ({{langx|el|Νικόλαος Α. Πέππας}}; born 25 August 1948, in [[Athens]], Greece) is a [[Chemical engineering|chemical]] and [[Biomedical engineering|biomedical engineer]] whose leadership in [[biomaterial|biomaterials science]] and [[engineering]], [[drug delivery]], [[bionanotechnology]], [[pharmaceutical sciences]], [[Chemical engineering|chemical]] and [[polymer engineering]] has provided seminal{{Promotion inline|date=August 2026}} foundations based on the physics and mathematical theories of nanoscale, macromolecular processes and drug/protein transport and has led to numerous biomedical products and devices.

==Education and work==
Peppas was educated in chemical engineering at the [[National Technical University of Athens]] ([[D. Eng.]], 1971) and at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] ([[Sc.D.]], 1973) under the direction of bioengineering pioneer Edward W. Merrill.<ref>[http://web.mit.edu/cheme/people/faculty/merrill.html Edward W. Merrill] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081218135408/http://web.mit.edu/cheme/people/faculty/merrill.html |date=18 December 2008 }}</ref> Subsequently, he was a postdoctoral fellow in the [[Arteriosclerosis]] Center of the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] under world biomedical leaders Clark K. Colton,<ref>[http://web.mit.edu/cheme/people/faculty/colton.html Clark K. Colton] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090223200340/http://web.mit.edu/cheme/people/faculty/colton.html |date=23 February 2009 }}</ref> Kenneth A. Smith<ref>[http://web.mit.edu/cheme/people/faculty/smith.html Kenneth A. Smith] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081218135418/http://web.mit.edu/cheme/people/faculty/smith.html |date=18 December 2008 }}</ref> and Robert S. Lees.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://hst.mit.edu/public/people/faculty/facultyBiosketch.jsp?key=Lees |title=Robert S. Lees |publisher=Hst.mit.edu |accessdate=2011-01-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110718102359/http://hst.mit.edu/public/people/faculty/facultyBiosketch.jsp?key=Lees |archive-date=2011-07-18 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He is the Cockrell Family Regents Chair #6 in [[Engineering]] at the [[University of Texas at Austin]]. He has been at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] since December 2002 and is serving as the director of the Institute of [[Biomaterials]], Drug Delivery, and Regenerative Medicine,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ibdr.engr.utexas.edu/|title=Home - IBDR|website=IBDR|accessdate=12 August 2017|archive-date=6 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151206063819/http://ibdr.engr.utexas.edu/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and its Laboratory of [[Biomaterials]], Drug Delivery and [[Bionanotechnology]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.che.utexas.edu/research/biomat/index.htm |title=Nicholas A. Peppas, Ph.D |publisher=Che.utexas.edu |accessdate=2011-01-04}}</ref> with appointments in the department of chemical engineering,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.che.utexas.edu/ |title=Department of Chemical Engineering - University of Texas at Austin |publisher=Che.utexas.edu |accessdate=2011-01-04}}</ref> the Department of Biomedical Engineering<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bme.utexas.edu/ |title=Department of Biomedical Engineering - University of Texas at Austin |publisher=Bme.utexas.edu |date=2010-05-31 |accessdate=2011-01-04}}</ref> and the College of [[Pharmacy]]<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.utexas.edu/pharmacy/general/directories/facultydir.html |title=University of Texas - College of Pharmacy - Austin Faculty Directory |publisher=Utexas.edu |date=2010-12-13 |accessdate=2011-01-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100602013839/http://www.utexas.edu/pharmacy/general/directories/facultydir.html |archive-date=2010-06-02 |url-status=dead }}</ref> at the [[University of Texas at Austin]]. Before 2002, he was the Showalter Distinguished Professor of Biomedical Engineering and professor of chemical engineering at [[Purdue University]].

Peppas is a [[researcher]] and [[inventor]] in the field of [[drug delivery]] and [[controlled release]]. He is also a leader in [[biomaterials]], [[bionanotechnology]], nano materials and bionanotechnology, and the fields of [[feedback|feedback controlled]] biomedical devices and molecular recognition.His contributions have been translated into more than twenty [[medicine|medical]] products.{{Citation needed|date=August 2026}}

Peppas is a member of the [[United States|US]] National Academy of Medicine,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://nam.edu/|title=- National Academy of Medicine|website=nam.edu|accessdate=12 August 2017}}</ref> the US [[National Academy of Engineering]] (NAE), the [http://www.academyofinventors.org/ National Academy of Inventors] (NAI), the [[:fr:Académie nationale de pharmacie|Académie Nationale of France]], the [https://www.academyofathens.gr/ Academy of Athens], the [[Real Academia Nacional de Farmacia]] of Spain and the Academy of [[Medicine]], [[Engineering]] and [[Sciences]] of Texas (TAMEST).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.tamest.org/about/ |title=The Academy of Medicine, Engineering and Science of Texas |publisher=TAMEST |accessdate=2011-01-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101009183511/http://www.tamest.org/about/ |archive-date=2010-10-09 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Very few chemical engineers are members of both NAE and IOM (including [[Frances Arnold]], [[Mark E. Davis|Mark Davis]], David Mooney of Harvard, and [[David A. Tirrell]] of the [[California Institute of Technology]], [[Rakesh Jain]] of [[Harvard]], [[Robert Langer]] of [[MIT]], and his former students [http://bioengineering.rice.edu/faculty/Antonios_Mikos.aspx Antonios Mikos] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170502203142/http://bioengineering.rice.edu/faculty/antonios_mikos.aspx |date=2017-05-02 }} of [[Rice University]] and [[Kristi Anseth]] of the University of Colorado).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.utexas.edu/news/2008/10/13/peppas_medicine/ |title=Pioneering Engineer Elected into Prestigious Institute of Medicine &#124; The University of Texas at Austin |publisher=Utexas.edu |accessdate=2011-01-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110425024316/http://www.utexas.edu/news/2008/10/13/peppas_medicine/ |archive-date=2011-04-25 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He has received [[honorary doctorate]]s from the [[University of Ghent]] (Belgium, 1999), the [[University of Parma]] (Italy, 2000), the [[National and Kapodistrian University of Athens]](Greece, 2000), the [[University of Ljubljana]] and the University of Patras (Greece, 2015) and an honorary professorship from [[Sichuan University]] (China, 2012).

He is [[President (corporate title)|president]] of the [[Fellow of Biomaterials Science and Engineering|International Union of Societies for Biomaterials Science and Engineering]] (2008–2016). He has served as a director of the [[Biomedical Engineering Society]] (2008–2011), Chair of the [https://web.archive.org/web/20081210005753/http://www.aimbe.org/content/index.php?pid=22 College of Fellows] of the [http://www.aimbe.org/ American Institute of Medical and Biological Engineering] (AIMBE, 2006–2007), President of the [http://www.biomaterials.org/ Society for Biomaterials] (SFB, 2003–2004), president of the [http://www.controlledrelease.org/ Controlled Release Society] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081225012951/http://www.controlledrelease.org/ |date=25 December 2008 }} (CRS, 1987–1988), director of the [[American Institute of Chemical Engineers]] ([http://www.aiche.org/ AIChE, 1999-2002]), chair of the engineering section of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS, 2014–15),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aaas.org/Section-M|title=Engineering (M)|date=19 June 2013|website=Aaas.org|accessdate=12 August 2017}}</ref> chairman of the materials division of AIChE <ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aiche.org/community/sites/divisions/mesd|title=Materials Engineering & Sciences Division (MESD)|website=Aiche.org|accessdate=12 August 2017|date=2014-05-22}}</ref> (1988–90) and director of the bioengineering division of AIChE <ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aiche.org/topics/biological-engineering|title=Biological Engineering|website=Aiche.org|accessdate=12 August 2017}}</ref> (1994–97). Peppas was Editor of the leading biomaterials science journal Biomaterials<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.elsevier.com/wps/find/journaldescription.cws_home/30392/description#description |title=Biomaterials |publisher=Elsevier |accessdate=2011-01-04}}</ref> from 1982 to 2002, an associate editor of the ''AIChE Journal'',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www3.interscience.wiley.com/journal/107061889/home/EditorialBoard.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130105062621/http://www3.interscience.wiley.com/journal/107061889/home/EditorialBoard.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=2013-01-05 |title=AIChE Journal|publisher=.interscience.wiley.com |accessdate=2011-01-04}}</ref> from 2009 to 2012, editor-in-chief of the Wiley/SFB Biomaterials Book Series (2006–2014), an associate editor of ''Biomedical Microdevices'',<ref>{{cite web|url=https://link.springer.com/journal/10544|title=Biomedical Microdevices - Springer|website=link.springer.com|accessdate=12 August 2017}}</ref> a consulting editor of ''Pharmaceutical Research''<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.aapspharmaceutica.com/publications/journal.asp?Journal=PHAM |title=AAPS Pharmaceutica |publisher=AAPS Pharmaceutica |accessdate=2011-01-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090208165712/http://aapspharmaceutica.com/publications/journal.asp?Journal=PHAM |archive-date=2009-02-08 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and an associate editor of the Cambridge University Press Biomedical Series.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cambridge.org/us/series/sSeries.asp?code=CTBE|title=Series - Cambridge University Press|website=Cambridge.org|accessdate=12 August 2017}}</ref>

He is an inaugural Fellow of the Biomedical Engineering Society, an inaugural Fellow of the [[Materials Research Society]] ([http://www.mrs.org/s_mrs/index.asp MRS] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110129054722/http://www.mrs.org/s_mrs/index.asp |date=29 January 2011 }}), an inaugural Fellow of the [http://www.controlledrelease.org/ CRS] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081225012951/http://www.controlledrelease.org/ |date=25 December 2008 }}, a founding Fellow of [http://www.aimbe.org/ AIMBE], a [http://portal.acs.org/portal/acs/corg/content?_nfpb=true&_pageLabel=PP_SUPERARTICLE&node_id=2246&use_sec=false&sec_url_var=region1&__uuid=e1e0a314-b899-48f4-bb1d-70745ab8bdff Fellow of the American Chemical Society], a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry]] (FRSC), [[Fellow of Biomaterials Science and Engineering|Fellow of the Society for Biomaterials]], a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]], a Fellow of the [https://web.archive.org/web/20081216014526/http://www.aapspharmaceutica.com/ American Association of Pharmaceutical Scientists] (AAPS), a Fellow of the [[American Institute of Chemical Engineers]], a [[Fellow of the AAAS|Fellow of the American Society for the Advancement of Science]] (AAAS), a Fellow of the [[American Society for Engineering Education]] (ASEE) and an Honorary fellow of the Italian Society of [[Medicine]] and [[Natural Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bibmed.unipr.it/Societa_di_medicina.htm |title=Società di Medicina |publisher=Bibmed.unipr.it |accessdate=2011-01-04 |archive-date=22 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722063652/http://www.bibmed.unipr.it/Societa_di_medicina.htm |url-status=dead }}</ref>

He has been a [[visiting professor]] at the [[University of Geneva]], [[University of Paris-Sud]] ([[Orsay]]/[[Chatenay-Malabry]]), [[University of Parma]], [[University of Pavia]], [[University of Naples Federico II]], [[Free University of Berlin]], [[University of Santiago de Compostela]], [[Complutense University of Madrid]], [[Hoshi University]], Tokyo, [[Hacettepe University]], Ankara, National and Kapodistrian [[University of Athens]], [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]], [[Nanyang Technological University]], Singapore, and the [[California Institute of Technology]].

Peppas is a leading scientist of modern [[drug delivery]]. He has helped to set the fundamentals and rational design of drug delivery systems and biomaterials over the past 39 years. He was the first to set the theories and equations that led to the design of a wide range of new systems. For example, using biomedical engineering principles and new biomedical transport theories, Peppas developed the equations that describe [[Fickian|Fickian and non-Fickian diffusion]] of drugs, peptides and proteins in [[controlled release]] devices. The "[https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=c17D_ggAAAAJ&view_op=list_works&pagesize=100 Peppas equation]" has become the standard method of analysis of pharmaceutical formulations or systems.<ref>[http://www.aimbe.org/content/index.php?pid=419]{{dead link|date=January 2011}}</ref> His earliest work also led to the development of a number of swelling-controlled release devices for the release of small molecular weight drugs. Using the modeling similarities of phase [[erosion]] and state erosion, he developed a unified model for all drug delivery systems.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Peppas | first1 = N.A. | last2 = Lustig | first2 = S.R. | year = 1985 | title = The Role of Crosslinks, Entanglements and Relaxations of the Macromolecular Carrier in the Diffusional Release of Biologically Active Materials: Conceptual and Scaling Relationships | journal = Ann. N.Y. Acad. Sci. | volume = 446 | pages = 26–41 | doi=10.1111/j.1749-6632.1985.tb18388.x| pmid = 3860156 | s2cid = 6808615 }}</ref> Similarly, he developed the theoretical framework for the analysis of transport through [[Cross-link|crosslinked]] biomaterials (the Peppas-Reinhart theory),<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Peppas | first1 = N.A. | last2 = Reinhart | first2 = C.T. | year = 1983 | title = Solute diffusion in swollen membranes. Part I: A new theory | journal = J. Membr. Sci. | volume = 15 | issue = 3| pages = 275–287 | doi=10.1016/s0376-7388(00)82304-2}}</ref> [[ion]]ic [[hydrogels]] (the Brannon-Peppas theory),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://mitocw.udsm.ac.tz/OcwWeb/Biological-Engineering-Division/BE-462JMolecular-Principles-of-BiomaterialsSpring2003/LectureNotes/index.htm|archive-url=https://archive.today/20070610072804/http://mitocw.udsm.ac.tz/OcwWeb/Biological-Engineering-Division/BE-462JMolecular-Principles-of-BiomaterialsSpring2003/LectureNotes/index.htm|url-status=dead|title=MIT OpenCourseWare - Biological Engineering Division - BE.462J Molecu…|date=10 June 2007|archive-date=10 June 2007|accessdate=12 August 2017}}</ref> and [[gel]]-[[Tissue (biology)|tissue]] interactions via [[tether]]s (the Huang-Peppas theory<ref>Y Huang, W Leobandung, A Foss and N.A Peppas, Molecular aspects of muco- and bioadhesion: tethered structures and site-specific surfaces, J. Control. Release 65, 63–71 (2000)</ref> and the Sahlin-Peppas equation<ref>J.J. Sahlin and N.A. Peppas, Enhanced hydrogel adhesion by polymer interdiffusion: Use of linear poly(ethylene glycol) as an adhesion promoter, ''J. Biomat Sci, Polym Ed'', 8, 421-436 (1997)</ref>). For the profound impact of these theories and analyses, Peppas has been recognized as the most cited and highly published [[author]] in "drug delivery", "biomaterials and drug delivery", and "intelligent materials". He is listed as a [http://isihighlycited.com/ Highly Cited Researcher<sup>SM</sup>] of Thomson Scientific and the Institute of Scientific Information.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://hcr3.isiknowledge.com/author.cgi?&link1=Search&link2=Search%20Results&AuthLastName=peppas&AuthFirstName=&AuthMiddleName=&AuthMailnstName=&CountryID=-1&DisciplineID=0&id=6361 |title=[ISI Highly Cited Researchers Version 1.5&#93; |publisher=Hcr3.isiknowledge.com |accessdate=2011-01-04}}</ref> He has also ranked as the most cited chemical <ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&view_op=search_authors&mauthors=chemical+engineering|title=Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.com|accessdate=12 August 2017}}</ref> and biomedical engineer <ref>{{cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&view_op=search_authors&mauthors=biomedical+engineering|title=Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.com|accessdate=12 August 2017}}</ref> with 106,026 [https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=c17D_ggAAAAJ&view_op=list_works&pagesize=100 citations] and an [[H-index]] of 152.

Applications of his theories and mathematical models have had a profound effect in the field.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.emergenttechnologies.com/eti_brief_2007.pdf |title= Interview with Dr. Nicholas Peppas |work=ETI Business Brief |date=Spring 2007 |publisher=Emergent Technologies Inc. |access-date=2008-12-31 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110710185947/http://www.emergenttechnologies.com/eti_brief_2007.pdf |archive-date=2011-07-10 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Peppas and his students originated the novel muco- and bioadhesive systems that interact molecularly with the [[mucus]] and [[Tissue (biology)|tissue]] and have been able to prolong bioavailability of [[proteins]] and [[peptides]] in the [[blood]]. As a result of his work, a number of biomedical [[polymers]] and commercial delivery devices have been launched. Peppas was the first to develop novel toxic-free [[poly(vinyl alcohol)]] gels by the [[freezing]]-[[thawing]] technique in 1975.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Peppas | first1 = N.A. | year = 1975 | title = Turbidimetric studies of aqueous poly(vinyl alcohol) solutions | journal = Makromol. Chem. | volume = 176 | issue = 11| pages = 3433–3440 | doi = 10.1002/macp.1975.021761125 }}</ref> These gels became very successful [[Joint|articular]] [[cartilage]] replacement systems.<ref>N.A. Peppas: "Hydrogels for Synthetic Articular Cartilage Applications," SPE Techn. Papers (NATEC), 62-63 (1977)</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Peppas | first1 = N. A. | year = 1979 | title = Characterization of homogeneous and pseudocomposite homopolymers and copolymers for articular cartilage replacement | journal = Biomaterials, Medical Devices, and Artificial Organs | volume = 7 | issue = 3| pages = 421–33 | doi=10.3109/10731197909119388| pmid = 476258 }}</ref> In 1978, he developed the same systems for ''in situ'' replacement of [[vocal cords]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Peppas | first1 = N.A. | last2 = Benner Jr | first2 = R.E. | year = 1980 | title = Method of intracordal injection and gelation of poly (vinyl alcohol) solution in vocal cords | journal = Biomaterials | volume = 1 | issue = 3| pages = 158–62 | doi=10.1016/0142-9612(80)90039-3| pmid = 7470568 }}</ref> In 1979 his group pioneered the use of [[hydrogels]] in drug delivery applications, including [[Epidermis (zoology)|epidermal]] bioadhesive systems<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Mongia | first1 = N.K. | last2 = Anseth | first2 = K.S. | last3 = Peppas | first3 = N.A. | year = 1996 | title = Mucoadhesive Poly(vinyl alcohol) Hydrogels Produced by Freezing/Thawing Processes: Applications in the Development of Wound Healing Systems | journal = J. Biomat. Sci., Polym. Ed. | volume = 7 | issue = 12| pages = 1055–1064 | doi=10.1163/156856296x00543| pmid = 8880437 }}</ref> and systems for the release of [[theophylline]],<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Korsmeyer | first1 = R.W. | last2 = Peppas | first2 = N.A. | year = 1981 | title = Effect of the Morphology of Hydrophilic Polymeric Matrices on the Diffusion and Release of Water Soluble Drugs | journal = J. Membr. Sci. | volume = 9 | issue = 3| pages = 211–227 | doi=10.1016/s0376-7388(00)80265-3}}</ref> proxyphylline, [[diltiazem]], and [[oxprenolol]].<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Gurny | first1 = R. | last2 = Peppas | first2 = N.A. | last3 = Harrington | first3 = D.D. | last4 = Banker | first4 = G.S. | year = 1981 | title = Development of Biodegradable and Injectable Latices for Controlled Release of Potent Drugs | journal = Drug Dev Ind Pharm | volume = 7 | pages = 1–25 | doi=10.3109/03639048109055684}}</ref> Peppas' [[laboratory|lab]] has developed new [[technology|technologies]] of oral delivery systems for [[insulin]] and other proteins.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Peppas | first1 = N.A. | year = 2004 | title = Devices based on intelligent biopolymers for oral protein delivery | journal = International Journal of Pharmaceutics | volume = 277 | issue = 1–2| pages = 11–17 | doi=10.1016/j.ijpharm.2003.03.001| pmid = 15158964<!-- deprecated | citeseerx = 10.1.1.383.9497 --> }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.pharmamanufacturing.com/articles/2005/217.html |title=Diabetes & Insulin: Beyond the Injection? &#124; Pharmaceutical Manufacturing |publisher=Pharmamanufacturing.com |date=2005-03-17 |accessdate=2011-01-04 |archive-date=15 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110715074425/http://www.pharmamanufacturing.com/articles/2005/217.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> These devices release insulin orally, "protecting" the insulin throughout its transport in the [[stomach]], upper [[small intestine]], and, eventually, blood, and bypassing [[diabetes|diabetics']] need for several daily injections.<ref>{{cite web |first=Brooke |last=Borel |url=http://www.cosmosmagazine.com/news/1966/insulin-pills-could-cut-need-needles |title=Insulin pills could cut the need for needles |publisher=COSMOS magazine |date=2008-05-02 |accessdate=2011-01-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110605172348/http://www.cosmosmagazine.com/news/1966/insulin-pills-could-cut-need-needles |archive-date=2011-06-05 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.diabetelibero.net/Novita-file-article-sid-967.html |title=Sanità: creato gel per insulina direttamente nell'intestino Ricerca Diabete Libero, un punto fermo in mare aperto |publisher=Diabetelibero.net |date=2008-04-22 |accessdate=2011-01-04 |archive-date=23 July 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110723091138/http://www.diabetelibero.net/Novita-file-article-sid-967.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> The same technology has been used for the transmucosal (oral, buccal) delivery of [[calcitonin]] (for treatment of [[osteoporosis]] in [[Postmenopause|postmenopausal]] women)<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Torres-Lugo | first1 = M. | last2 = Garcia | first2 = M. | last3 = Record | first3 = R. | last4 = Peppas | first4 = N.A. | year = 2002 | title = Physicochemical Behavior and Cytotoxic Effects of P(MAA-g-EG) Nanospheres for Oral Delivery of Proteins | url = https://zenodo.org/record/1259907| journal = Journal of Controlled Release | volume = 80 | issue = 1–3| pages = 197–205 | doi=10.1016/s0168-3659(02)00027-5| pmid = 11943398 }}</ref> and [[interferon-alpha]] (for [[cancer therapy]]), and is being investigated for [[interferon-beta]] release for [[multiple sclerosis|multiple sclerotic]] patients.<ref>{{citation |first=Robert |last=Neal |url=http://archives.focus.hms.harvard.edu/2004/July16_2004/nanotech.html |title=Nano and Stem Cells: Crossroads Technologies Mapped at Korea Conference |publisher=[[Harvard University]] |date=2004-07-16 |accessdate=2013-03-16 |archive-date=6 September 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140906133715/http://archives.focus.hms.harvard.edu/2004/July16_2004/nanotech.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Peppas was one of the pioneers of intelligent biomaterials, and medical devices. Using intelligent polymers<ref>N.A. Peppas and LS. Flosenzier (1986) ''Life Support Syst.'', 4 (Suppl. 2) 395</ref><ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Brannon-Peppas | first1 = L. | last2 = Peppas | first2 = N.A. | year = 1990 | title = Dynamic and equilibrium swelling behaviour of pH-sensitive hydrogels containing 2-hydroxyethyl methacrylate | doi = 10.1016/0142-9612(90)90021-h | pmid = 2090297 | journal = Biomaterials | volume = 11 | issue = 9| pages = 635–44 }}</ref> as early as 1980, Peppas and his group were the first to use such [[pH]]-sensitive and [[temperature]]-sensitive systems for modulated release of [[streptokinase]] and other [[fibrinolysis|fibrinolytic]] [[enzymes]].

Peppas has founded three companies: Mimetic Solutions, Appian Labs and CoraDyn Biosystems for the commercialization of various [[pharmaceutics|pharmaceutical]] products and medical devices. He is the author of 1,450 publications, and numerous proceedings papers and abstracts, with more than 80,000 citations and an [https://scholar.google.com/citations?hl=en&user=c17D_ggAAAAJ&view_op=list_works&pagesize=100 H-index of 135]. He is the coauthor or coeditor of 37 books, including the three-volume ''Hydrogels in Medicine and Pharmacy'' (CRC Press, 1987),<ref>{{cite book|title=Hydrogels in Medn & PHARM Vol 2 (Hydrogels in Medicine & Pharmacy) (9780849355479): Nicholas A. Peppas: Books |date= 31 January 1987|isbn = 978-0849355479|last1= Peppas|first1= N. A.|publisher= CRC-Press}}</ref> the [[monograph]] ''Pulsatile Drug Delivery'' (WSGS, Stuttgart, 1993), two books on [[Biopolymers]] (Springer, 1994), the monograph ''Molecular and Cellular Foundations of Biomaterials'' (Academic Press, 2004<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bookfinder.com/dir/i/Molecular_and_Cellular_Foundations_of_Biomaterials/0120085291/ |title=Advances in Chemical Engineering Vol. 29 : Molecular and Cellular Foundations of Biomaterials (0120085291) by Nicholas Peppas, Michael J. Sefton @ |publisher=Bookfinder.com |accessdate=2011-01-04 |archive-date=8 June 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608005241/http://www.bookfinder.com/dir/i/Molecular_and_Cellular_Foundations_of_Biomaterials/0120085291/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>), the book ''Intelligent Therapeutics: Biomimetic Systems and Nanotechnology in Drug Delivery'' (Elsevier, 2004), the monograph ''Nanotechnology in Therapeutics'' (Horizon Press, 2007<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.google.com/products/catalog?hl=en&q=peppas+books&cid=4993513825740220296#ps-sellers |title=Nanotechnology in therapeutics: current technology and applications [Book&#93; |accessdate=2011-01-04}}</ref>) and the book ''Chronobiology and Drug Delivery'' (Elsevier, 2007).

==Awards==
He has been awarded more than 150 national and international [[awards]]. These include:
* the [https://sepsg.org/HongKong24/ BMEMat Lifetime Achievement Award Winner (2024)]
*the [http://www.nae.edu/Activities/Projects/Awards/FoundersAwards/FoundersWinners.aspx Founders Award of the National Academy of Engineering (2012)] 
*the highest distinction from the [http://www.aimbe.org/ American Institute of Medical and Biological Engineering] (the Pierre Galletti Award<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aimbe.org/content/index.php?pid=88|title=American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering - Galletti Awards|date=10 December 2008|accessdate=12 August 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081210005956/http://www.aimbe.org/content/index.php?pid=88|archive-date=10 December 2008}}</ref> (2008))<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aimbe.org/press/details.php?id=415&pid=20&tpid=1|date=20 August 2008|accessdate=12 August 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080820062144/http://www.aimbe.org/press/details.php?id=415&pid=20&tpid=1|archive-date=20 August 2008|title=American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering - Featured News }}</ref> and the Pritzker Lecture (2016)
*the highest distinctions of the [http://www.biomaterials.org/ Society for Biomaterials] (the Founders Award for Lifetime Contributions<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.bme.utexas.edu/news/2004_peppas.cfm |title=Professor N. A. Peppas receives the Founders Award of the Society for Biomaterials - News Archive: 2002-2004 - News - Department of Biomedical Engineering - University of Texas at Austin |publisher=Bme.utexas.edu |accessdate=2011-01-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110720104800/http://www.bme.utexas.edu/news/2004_peppas.cfm |archive-date=2011-07-20 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.biomaterials.org/past_awardees.cfm#2005 |title=Society for Biomaterials - Past Awardees |publisher=Biomaterials.org |accessdate=2011-01-04 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121231213000/http://www.biomaterials.org/past_awardees.cfm#2005 |archive-date=2012-12-31 }}</ref> (2005), the William Hall Award for Service (2010) and the Clemson Award for Basic Research<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.biomaterials.org/past_awardees.cfm#1992 |title=Society for Biomaterials - Past Awardees |publisher=Biomaterials.org |accessdate=2011-01-04 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121231213000/http://www.biomaterials.org/past_awardees.cfm#1992 |archive-date=2012-12-31 }}</ref> (1992))

*the highest recognition from the Southeastern Universities Research Association (SURA Distinguished Scientist Award (2010))
*the International Award, European Society for Biomaterials (2015) 
*the Giulio Natta Medal, from the Polytechnic School of Milan, Italy (2014) 
*the highest research recognitions from the [[American Institute of Chemical Engineers]] (the Founders Award <ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aiche.org/About/Awards/AwardforOutstandingContributions.aspx |title=AIChE |publisher=AIChE |accessdate=2011-01-04 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101104090510/http://www.aiche.org/About/Awards/AwardforOutstandingContributions.aspx |archive-date=2010-11-04 }}</ref> (2008), the 59th Institute Lecture<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aiche.org/IAbout/Awards/Committee/InstituteLecturer.aspx |title=AIChE |publisher=AIChE |accessdate=2011-01-04}}</ref> (2007), the William Walker Award<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aiche.org/About/Awards/WilliamHWalkerAward.aspx |title=AIChE |publisher=AIChE |accessdate=2011-01-04}}</ref> (2006)) as well as the Nanoscale Science and Engineering Award (2014), the Food, Pharmaceuticals and Bioengineering Award<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aiche.org/About/Awards/Divisions/FoodPharmaceuticalBioengineeringDivisionAwardChemicalEngineering.aspx |title=AIChE |publisher=AIChE |accessdate=2011-01-04}}</ref> (1991) and the CMA Stine Materials Science and Engineering Award<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aiche.org/About/Awards/Divisions/CharlesMAStineAward.aspx |title=AIChE |publisher=AIChE |date=2010-02-15 |accessdate=2011-01-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101104092416/http://www.aiche.org/About/Awards/Divisions/CharlesMAStineAward.aspx |archive-date=2010-11-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref> (1984)

*the highest recognitions of the [[American Society for Engineering Education]] (the 2013 Benjamin Garver Lamme Excellence in Engineering Education Award, the 2000 General Electric Senior Research Award recognizing the best engineering researcher of the USA<ref name="archive.org">{{cite web|url=http://asee.org/activities/awards/archive/national1.cfm?&printerFriendly=|date=12 December 2007|accessdate=12 August 2017|title=Past National Award Winners|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071212000213/http://asee.org/activities/awards/archive/national1.cfm?&printerFriendly=|archive-date=12 December 2007}}</ref>), as well as the 1992 George Westinghouse Award recognizing the best teacher,<ref name="archive.org"/> the 1988 Curtis McGraw Award for best engineering research under the age of 40,<ref name="archive.org"/> and the 2006 Dow Chemical Engineering Award
*the 2002 Newsmaker of the Year Award of the [[American Chemical Society]]

In addition, he has received the highest scientific recognitions from both Universities with which he has been associated:

*the 2004 Hamilton Award for best paper from the University of Texas at Austin
*the 2002 [[Sigma Xi]] Award for Best Research from Purdue University<ref>{{cite web |url=https://engineering.purdue.org/BME/AboutUs/News/2002/march_20_html |title=Professor Nicholas A. Peppas to Receive Sigma Xi Faculty Research Award - Biomedical Engineering, Purdue University |publisher=Engineering.purdue.org |date=2002-03-20 |accessdate=2011-01-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110727191426/https://engineering.purdue.org/BME/AboutUs/News/2002/march_20_html |archive-date=2011-07-27 |url-status=dead }}</ref>
*the 2000 McCoy Award<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.purdue.edu/research/vpr/funding/research_awards.shtml|title=VPR|date=20 December 2008|accessdate=12 August 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081220230519/http://www.purdue.edu/research/vpr/funding/research_awards.shtml|archive-date=20 December 2008}}</ref> from Purdue University (second engineer in the 40-year history of the award)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.purdue.edu/research/vpr/funding/peppas.shtml|title=VPR|date=12 October 2008|accessdate=12 August 2017|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081012125829/http://www.purdue.edu/research/vpr/funding/peppas.shtml|archive-date=12 October 2008}}</ref>

In 2008 he was selected as one of the 100 Engineers of the Modern Era by the [[American Institute of Chemical Engineers]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aiche.org/about/centennial/engineers.aspx |title=Historic and Modern Era Engineers |publisher=AIChE |accessdate=2011-01-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080309110025/http://www.aiche.org/about/centennial/engineers.aspx |archive-date=2008-03-09 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 1991, the [[Magazine|journal]] Polymer News recognized him as a polymer pioneer. Finally, in 2002, he was recognized as a biomedical pioneer<ref>{{cite journal|pmid=12119875 | volume=21 | issue=3 | title=Voices of experience. Interview by Frederik Nebeker and Michael Geselowitz | year=2002 | journal=IEEE Eng Med Biol Mag | pages=48–89 | doi=10.1109/memb.2002.1016852 | last1 = Arzbaecher | first1 = R | last2 = Babb | first2 = A | last3 = Bailey | first3 = J |display-authors=etal }}</ref> by the [[IEEE]] Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society.

==Researchers under his supervision==
Peppas has supervised more than 875 researchers, visiting [[scientists]] and graduate [[students]] including 100 [[PhD]]s, of which 54 are now professors in other universities. Many others have become leading biomedical scientists, [[engineers]], [[physicians]] and medical [[professionals]]. Peppas' former students are affectionately called "peppamers".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.che.utexas.edu/research/biomat/images/peppamerletter.jpg|title=Nicholas A. Peppas, Sc.D.|website=Che.utexas.edu|accessdate=12 August 2017}}</ref> Among the numerous graduates from his laboratories, there are some of the leaders of [[drug delivery]], [[biomaterials]], [[bionanotechnology]], [[polymer science]] and pharmaceutical sciences including the [[United States National Academy of Engineering|NAE]], [[National Academy of Sciences|NAS]] and [[Institute of Medicine|IOM]] member, and [[HHMI]] Investigator Kristi Anseth of the [[University of Colorado at Boulder|University of Colorado]]; the NAE/IOM member and [[Alpha Chi Sigma]], BMES and SFB Clemson awards recipient Antonios Mikos of Rice University; the NAE member Richard Korsmeyer of Pfizer, the NAE member John Klier of the Dow Chemical Company; the AIChE Colburn, Wilhelm and SFB Clemson awards ==Personal life==
Nicholas Peppas is married to Lisa Brannon-Peppas,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://engineering.purdue.edu/ChE/HomepageFeatures/LisaBrannonPeppasreceivedthe2008ChemicalEngineering |title=Homepage Features - Chemical Engineering, Purdue University |publisher=Engineering.purdue.edu |accessdate=2011-01-04}}</ref> whom he met at Purdue University, where she was doing her Ph.D. in chemical engineering. They have two children, Katherine and Alexander. They reside in Austin, Texas. Peppas' extracurricular activities include writing about the history of [[chemical engineering]], opera, history and other subjects. He has published books<ref>[https://books.google.com/books?id=lFXHVTDLIegC&dq=peppas+history+of+chemical+engineering+kluwer&pg=PA1 ] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140914164050/http://books.google.com/books?id=lFXHVTDLIegC&pg=PA1&lpg=PA1&dq=peppas+history+of+chemical+engineering+kluwer&source=bl&ots=_KyFpzoSh_&sig=4rUVXvw2eUb1oY2fCJihdPGc7WA&hl=en&sa=X&oi=book_result&resnum=1&ct=result |date=2014-09-14 }}</ref> and review articles<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pafko.com/history/h_bib.html |title=History of ChEn: Bibliography |publisher=Pafko.com |accessdate=2011-01-04}}</ref> on the subject. His review of the Centennial of AIChE was published by the [[Chemical Heritage Foundation]] in August 2008.<ref name=Peppas>{{cite journal|last1=Peppas|first1=Nicholas A.|title=The First Century of Chemical Engineering|journal=Chemical Heritage Magazine|date=2008|volume=26|issue=3|pages=26–29|url=https://www.sciencehistory.org/distillations/article/first-century-chemical-engineering|accessdate=20 March 2018}}</ref>
Peppas is also an avid record collector and author of biographies and monographs on opera.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_qa5350/is_200002/ai_n21451983/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091002121446/http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_qa5350/is_200002/ai_n21451983/ | url-status=usurped | archive-date=2 October 2009 | work=Chemical Engineering Progress | title=Chemical engineers with many loves and a social conscience: Profile of a husband and wife team | year=2000}}</ref> A book on the Greek tenor ''Vasso Argyris: The Great Greek Tenor of the Interwar Years'' was published in 2008.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.utexas.edu/friends/popups/spotlight_92.html |title=Quick Facts on Nicholas A. Peppas |accessdate=2009-01-13 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100528233815/http://www.utexas.edu/friends/popups/spotlight_92.html |archive-date=2010-05-28 }}</ref>

He has also written numerous biographies on Greek opera singers including the tenor of La Scala Nicola Filacuridi (1924–2009), the soprano of the Paris Opera Elen Dosia (1913–2002), the celebrated Greek tenor Michael Theodore (1939–) who had a radio and record career in Germany, the lyric tenor Antonios Delendas (1902–1966), the celebrated Greek soprano of the Scala di Milano Rena Gary Falachi, (Rena Garyfallaki, 1920–), the bass Petros Hoidas (1914–1977), the tenor of the Vienna State Opera Petros Baxevanos (1904–1982), the tenor of the Lyric Opera of Athens Nikos Hatzinikolaou (1929–), the internationally known Greek singers Nicola Zaccaria (1923–2007), Nicola Moscona (1907–1975), Kostas Paskalis (1929–2007), Efthymios Mihalopoulos (1937–), and Pavlos Raptis (1938–) and many others.{{citation needed|date=March 2025}}
